clue.text: Judge dressed for court put back sympathetic expression

indicators.note: put back tells us the word for court dress is to be read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: a barrister or judge going into court is robed
ah is a soft cry of sympathy

explanation.surface: A judge, gowned for the courtroom, offers a murmur of sympathy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is not a verb or a court official but the biblical judge of Israel; 'put back' reverses the courtroom word.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament Book of Judges she is the prophetess who judged Israel.

clue.text: Agitate to shake off blossom?

parts.note: the prefix dis- means to remove or undo
may is hawthorn blossom

explanation.surface: A whimsical question: what do you call stripping a tree of its flowers?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey reading: to dis-may a hawthorn is to strip its may blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay is to upset or perturb someone, a synonym for agitate.

clue.text: Slipped into unconsciousness, having lost fluid all round

indicators.note: all round says the bleeding word encloses the other piece

parts.note: bled means lost blood
under, as in going under an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A patient lapsing into a coma after heavy blood loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slipped' looks like part of the medical scene but is the definition: made a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: To blunder is to make a careless mistake, which is what slipping up means.

clue.text: Old style corps heading off secretarial firm

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

indicators.note: heading off says the firm loses its first letter

parts.note: an agency supplies temporary secretaries

explanation.surface: An army unit setting off for an old-fashioned typing pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Regency was a period style of furniture and architecture from early nineteenth-century Britain.

clue.text: Shakespeare's general Henry calls for attention to hold ballot

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: to hold says the two cries enclose the vote

parts.note: oi is a shout to get someone's attention
a second oi, since 'calls' is plural
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean military leader named Henry shouting for silence before a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, 'caviare to the general' uses 'general' for the common people. 'Henry' is not a king but H, the unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's 'the general' means the masses, the common people, which this Greek phrase denotes.

clue.text: Shield that can't withstand a blow?

definitions.meaning: a small round shield held in the hand by a strap
playfully, something that buckles, crumpling when struck

explanation.surface: A piece of armour that is useless against attack.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading coins a noun from the verb 'buckle': one that buckles, gives way, under a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round hand-held shield from medieval combat bears this name.

clue.text: Significant part of Bible for sectarian

parts.note: big means important or significant
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A large chunk of scripture used to support a narrow sect's views.
explanation.definitionFit: A sectarian person is narrow-minded and intolerant of other creeds, as a bigot is.

clue.text: Ticket provided free at first for City

parts.note: a card can serve as a ticket or pass
if means provided that

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of free

explanation.surface: A ticket given away gratis for a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Wales is a major British city.

clue.text: One doing much like Gill needs one skirt

parts.note: a lung, like a fish's gill, is a breathing organ
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone resembling a woman named Gill needs a skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gill' with a capital looks like a woman's name but is the fish's breathing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth wrapped round the waist and worn in South Asia, like a sarong.

clue.text: Got fat from deer, carved up in distress

indicators.note: in places the jumbled animal inside the word for distress

parts.note: to rend is to tear apart or cause anguish, as in heart-rending

indicators.note: carved up, cut to pieces, signals the letters of deer are rearranged

explanation.surface: A butcher extracting fat from venison while upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carved up' rearranges DEER as DERE, set 'in' REND.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendering fat is melting it down from animal tissue to extract the lard or dripping.

clue.text: Getting pounds in small robbery and running

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: in places the pounds sign inside the word for street robbery

parts.note: mugging is robbery in the street
L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Someone getting money from a petty street robbery and then fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' is not fleeing but the trade sense, as in gun-running: carrying contraband. 'Getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Running goods is moving contraband illegally across a border, as in rum-running.

clue.text: Argument results in arrest

definitions.meaning: police run a suspect in, taking them into custody

explanation.surface: A quarrel that ends with someone being taken into custody.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for a quarrel and a phrasal verb for taking someone into custody share these letters.

clue.text: The saint of Opera North

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera set in ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: Reads as the patron saint of the company Opera North, based in Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Opera North is a real English opera company, so the clue seems a single name; split it into the opera and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish monk who founded the monastery at Lindisfarne in Northumbria is venerated as a saint.

clue.text: Heading for trouble, flogging nicotine round hospital

indicators.note: round shows the jumbled letters go around the hospital letter
flogging, beating about, signals that the letters of nicotine are to be jumbled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone selling cigarettes on a hospital ward is asking for trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flogging' looks like selling, but it rearranges NICOTINE to ONTINICE, and 'round' puts it around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on thin ice is an idiom for being in a risky position likely to bring trouble.

clue.text: Service briefly offered a long way back

definitions.text: Service briefly offered a long way back

parts.words: Service briefly offered a long way back
parts.note: the armed service's three-letter abbreviation is the word for a long way, read backwards

explanation.surface: A service once available but long since discontinued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a long way' is FAR; 'back' reverses it to RAF, which is the 'briefly' (abbreviated) form of the 'Service' named in full in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's air arm is one of its three armed services, usually shortened to three initials.

clue.text: Not knowing region, can get confused

indicators.note: get confused means the letters of the two words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Lacking local knowledge, one can easily lose one's bearings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is the state of lacking knowledge, being unaware.

clue.text: Sent down as papal representative, dressed as cardinal?

indicators.note: dressed says the envoy is clothed in the colour

parts.note: cardinal red is the bright red of a cardinal's robes
a legate is an envoy of the Pope

explanation.surface: A papal envoy dispatched in a cardinal's robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent down' suggests expulsion from university, but here it is demotion.
explanation.definitionFit: A team relegated is moved to a lower division; demoted, sent down.

clue.text: Membrane found defective in a primate

indicators.note: defective, faulty, signals the letters of a primate are rearranged

explanation.surface: A faulty membrane discovered in an ape or monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The delicate innermost membrane enveloping the brain and spinal cord.

clue.text: Transformative device suggesting a twist of logic?

parts.note: induction is reasoning from particular cases to a general rule
a coil is a spiral twist, as of rope or wire

explanation.surface: A gadget that seems to embody some twisted reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'a twist of logic' as a coil of induction: the twist comes first in the clue but second in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This apparatus is a transformer that steps up low voltage into high-voltage pulses.

clue.text: Rabbit caught by predator

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a hunter preys on other animals

explanation.surface: A rabbit seized by a fox or hawk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is not the animal but British slang for chatter (rabbit on).
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean to talk at length, grumbling or prattling, in informal British usage.

clue.text: One goes round showing gold tooth perhaps

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a tooth is one example of something that bites

explanation.surface: Someone flashing a gold tooth as they make their rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft or satellite that circles a planet is called this.

clue.text: Little space in particularly attractive meeting

indicators.note: in places the small printing space inside the desirable word

parts.note: a plum job is an especially desirable one
an en is a printer's space half the width of an em

explanation.surface: A bit of room in an especially appealing gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A plenum is a full assembly attended by all members, a type of meeting.

clue.text: 24th June 2000?

definitions.meaning: the feast of St John the Baptist, the traditional quarter day at the height of the warm season
the middle letters of the season's name are MM, Roman numerals for two thousand

explanation.surface: Looks like a date: the twenty-fourth of June in the millennium year.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: the centre of SUMMER is MM, the Roman 2000, so 2000 is mid-summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Midsummer Day, a quarter day in England, falls on the twenty-fourth of June.

clue.text: Waitress ordered to bag up refuse

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says those hidden letters read from bottom to top
to bag means to contain, so the letters sit inside the two words

explanation.surface: A waitress is told to put rubbish into a sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bag' holds SSORD across Waitress ordered; 'up' turns it to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is waste matter, rubbish, as refuse (the noun) is.

clue.text: Doctor has struggle to get one screened

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
to vie is to compete or struggle

explanation.surface: A doctor fighting to get a patient tested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screened' suggests medical screening, but means shown on a screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is something shown on a cinema screen.

clue.text: Roll as sailor around lake

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the pair of pieces before it the other way round

parts.note: eg, for example, can stand for as in 'such as'
AB is an able seaman, a sailor
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A sailor rolling as he steps about by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses EGAB to BAGE; L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped bread roll, boiled then baked, goes by this name.

clue.text: Profiteer has 10 fish

indicators.note: has signals that the profiteer contains the next piece

parts.note: a tout resells tickets at inflated prices
the answer at 10 across is RUN-IN, so R, short for run in cricket, goes in

explanation.surface: A racketeer is holding ten fish.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is a cross-reference to 10 across: read 'has run in', so R (run) goes inside TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater game fish of the salmon family, prized by anglers.

clue.text: A number of the French gamble

definitions.meaning: the card game also called pontoon or blackjack, played for stakes

explanation.surface: A French figure risked on a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: The French for twenty-one names the card game where players aim for that total.

clue.text: Coolness of one that hasn't made the team

definitions.text: one that hasn't made the team
definitions.meaning: a substitute player kept back from the starting side

explanation.surface: The aloofness of a player left out of the side.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a cool, restrained manner and a substitute player go by this word.

clue.text: Almost premature openings for mate on dangerous back rank

indicators.note: almost means the word for premature stops one letter short

parts.note: early means premature

indicators.note: back says those initial letters are to be read in reverse order
openings are the first letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A chess player threatened with premature mate on a perilous back rank.

explanation.definitionFit: The title and dignity of an earl is a rank in the British peerage.
